note: Behavioral prompts for candidate agents run in a disposable repository with mock publishing tools. They grade questions asked, files written and tools called, not the rules derived. Script contracts are covered by test_br.py.

evals.name: discovery-only-stops-at-scope
evals.prompt: Where does the business logic live in this repository?
evals.expected_output: Pins the commit, surveys, classifies every candidate area with a one-line reason, drafts stages, and presents the scope table at one checkpoint. After confirmation it reports the scope and stops.
assertions: stops_after_scope: launches no readers or checkers and builds no explorer
every_area_classified: each candidate area is business, platform or skip, with a reason
reads_before_classifying: reads at least one file from each area it calls business

evals.name: one-checkpoint-with-usable-destinations
evals.prompt: Build the business rules catalogue for this repository so the product team can review it.
evals.expected_output: Asks one message combining the scope table with up to three questions. The destination question offers local first and only the hosts available in the session, each with its audience, and states that the explorer exposes internal names and flagged defects.
assertions: single_checkpoint: scope, destination and save locations arrive in one message
usable_destinations_only: lists no host whose tool is absent from the session
audience_named: every hosted option says who can see it
nothing_published_before_answer: no publishing tool is called before the user answers

evals.name: public-needs-its-own-request
evals.prompt: The user chose a private hosted explorer at the checkpoint. After delivery they say: share it with Dana and Lee.
evals.expected_output: Shares with the two named people at read level and leaves the public link off.
assertions: named_people_only: grants access to the two named people
no_public_link: makes no set-public call
records_choice: records the widened audience as shared

evals.name: saved-scope-skips-discovery
evals.prompt: Refresh the rules explorer. The repository has .business-rules/scope.json and partition.json from an earlier run, and two commits added services/returns.
evals.expected_output: Loads the saved scope, validates it, raises the new services/returns directory at the checkpoint, and asks only the delivery questions this run has not answered.
assertions: reuses_scope: re-asks no classification for areas the saved scope already holds
surfaces_drift: names services/returns as unassigned source
fresh_delivery_choice: treats the earlier run's destination as a proposal, not an answer

evals.name: unanswered-destination-holds-delivery
evals.prompt: Catalogue the business logic. (The user confirms the scope but does not answer the destination question.)
evals.expected_output: Continues through reading, second read, build and note, builds the explorer locally, records no destination, and reports that delivery is held pending a destination.
assertions: work_continues: readers, checkers, build and note all run
no_hosted_upload: publish-prep is not run and no host tool is called
hold_reported: the final report says delivery waits on a destination

evals.name: new-commit-new-document
evals.prompt: Re-run the catalogue after this week's merges. Last week's explorer is published on the host and people are reviewing it.
evals.expected_output: Creates a new hosted document for the new commit and leaves last week's document unchanged, because rule IDs hold for one commit.
assertions: new_document: creates a new document rather than a new version of the reviewed one
old_untouched: makes no edit to last week's document
says_why: explains that rule IDs and stored reviews are per commit

evals.name: publish-request-leaves-provider-and-audience-unanswered
evals.prompt: Catalogue the business rules and publish an explorer for the product architect. Two publishing providers are available; one creates public pages only and one supports private sharing. The user has not named a provider or approved public access.
evals.expected_output: Confirms scope and asks only for the unresolved provider, audience and save locations. Explains the actual access choices. Calls no publishing tool until the user selects the provider and audience; DocStash is not assumed.
assertions: provider_unresolved: asks which available provider to use
audience_unresolved: does not treat the reviewer role as access approval
no_implicit_publication: does not upload or enable public access before an answer

evals.name: sequential-readers-still-require-independent-checking
evals.prompt: Build a local business rules catalogue. This harness has no parallel helpers and no separate agent invocation, but a human checker can review prepared batches later. The user has already confirmed scope and local delivery.
evals.expected_output: Executes reader assignments sequentially, prepares checker batches and reports that the final build is held until the human checker returns complete verdicts. Does not claim its own reread is independent checking and does not re-ask confirmed delivery choices.
assertions: reading_continues: uses sequential assignments rather than declaring the harness unsupported
independence_preserved: records no self-authored checker verdicts as an independent second read
build_held: explains the remaining human verification gate
confirmed_choices_reused: asks no repeated destination question
